findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: There was a spatula observed on the top surface of the microwave oven. The food contact surface was in direct contact with the outside surface of the oven. Shown to person-in-charge (PIC) and the utensil was placed inside of a clean container for storage. Ensure that in use utensils are stored in a manner where they aren't exposed to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a written procedure on how to respond to vomit or diarrheal events posted at the facility. Inspector provided a copy of a Norovirus cleanup policy to make available for employees. Ensure that norovirus clean-up procedure is available.

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Employee was advised on proper technique. Ensure hands are dried prior to using paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet. If paper towels are used to shut off the faucet prior to drying hands, then discard the used paper towels and retrieve new paper towels to dry hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Ice scoop was observed with handle down in contact with ice in the bin of the ice machine. PIC noted the scoop is to be stored with the handle extended up out of ice and repositioned the scoop to allow for proper storage.
 Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of food thermometer was soiled with stuck on food debris. PIC removed soil and wiped down the food thermometer with sanitizer solution during inspection. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of food thermometer between uses.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. If quat solution is used to wipe stem after immediate use, ensure stem is cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Almond milk and whipped topping sitting out for use at room temperature had surface temperatures above 45F. Products were dispensed in cups to take internal temperatures and observed at 48F and 58F respectively. Products in question would be used or discarded in less than 4hrs. Cold holding versus time control were discussed. A time control policy was established during inspection (see general comments for additional information) .
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.
